correctness.rationale: Bochner L1 duality is valid because the separable finite Hilbert sum X is reflexive, so X* has RNP. Restriction fixes g; ℓq dual norm gives the complete pointwise ball field. Opposite measurable fields ±ae attain exact diameter. For arbitrary affine center k, the measurable antipodal choice attains the exact covering-radius formula esssup(a+||k||), from which the full center set and its uniqueness follow. The norm-attainment criterion follows from equality in the pointwise integral bound, with an explicit norming vector. A two-set piecewise-constant field realizes every claimed diameter and proves failure of wU; the one-atom case gives U, wU, SU. The zero functional is separately harmless and was not used in normalized statements.

value.rationale: A motivated 1<p<infinity Bochner preservation theorem leaves the L1 endpoint open. This result determines the entire exact endpoint extension fiber, its sharp diameter, all relative Chebyshev centers and the attainable diameter spectrum over every finite measure algebra for all ℓr direct-sum geometries. It separates maximal Hahn–Banach nonuniqueness from uniqueness of the optimal Chebyshev center at r=1, and gives a sharp global U/wU/SU boundary rather than just one counterexample. Although the proof uses classical duality and short inequalities, the full parameter classification is a natural operator-geometric invariant, not a routine numerical special case.
